$comment: The autonomy policy layer (issue #22, proposal C): each former human gate becomes a machine-decidable rule with a conservative default, journaled and non-blocking. Evaluated only in code (tools/pipeline.py resolve-gates / tools/state.py resolve-gate) — never by LLM self-approval. Every decision records decided_by='policy:<rule-id>' + policy_version + evidence[] in migration-state.json. Levels: L0 = supervised (gates are hard stops — the agent never asks; it leaves the gate open and ends the run with the dossier for the operator to decide between runs); L1 = agent proposes into the dossier, operator decides between runs; L2 = all gates policy-resolved, publish disabled (the default — never asks); L3 = full autopilot incl. cutover. Operators pre-authorize the level BEFORE the run: there are zero mid-run questions at any level. The dual-build design is what makes autonomy safe — per-unit Python fallback, one-env-var shim, rollback pin; every autonomous decision stays reversible per unit.

L0.name: supervised
L0.gates: hard stops, never questions — the agent (the stage checklists / MIGRATION_PROMPT.md) drives, leaves the gate open with journaled evidence, and ends the run with the dossier; the operator decides between runs

L1.name: assisted
L1.gates: agent proposes a resolution per gate into the dossier and ends the run; the operator applies or rejects it between runs — nothing asks mid-run

L2.name: autonomous
L2.gates: all gates resolved by the rules below in code — journaled, non-blocking, conservative defaults

L3.name: autopilot
L3.gates: as L2, plus Stage-6 cutover/publish once CUT-1's evidence bar is met

budget.$comment: Global ceilings enforced by the driver (tools/pipeline.py run) — the run-level analogue of the per-unit MAX_ROUNDS budget. Copy into state.autonomy.budget at init time; the state block wins once present. v1.4.0 (ADR design/0001, the single-session run model): these are the ONLY bounds that may stop a healthy run — a real migration is day-scale, so the ceilings are day-scale (7 days wall clock, 50M tokens). The driver recycles agent contexts per unit chunk, so no LLM context window ever bounds the run; max_agent_retries_per_unit bounds fresh-context retries of one unit chunk before ESC-1 defer. max_chain_depth (issue #25): session-level budget_exhausted under the GLV chain harness (tools/succession.py) ALWAYS spawns a successor — the harness bootstraps GLV itself (issue #47: it ensures `glv serve` is up and mints its own named token per session; no alternate transport, no human provisioning step); the cap bounds how many successions may chain (over it, or if a successor advances no observable state, the run ends failed_safely with the dossier). The ceilings bound the ENTIRE chain — token spend sums through the single migration-state.json, wall clock sums over sessions — so a fresh session budget never means a fresh run budget.

candidates.$comment: Issue #59 — K (MIGRATION_PROMPT.md hard rule 4) is policy, not judgment. The fixed 'K=3 for every unit' made the loop shape an improvisation under real budgets (a run used K=1 + oracle-ranked repair rounds and journaled a prose 'budget-driven deviation' note — a tradeoff every future run would re-make by hand). The schedule: K=k_small_unit below size_threshold_loc (cheap to parallelize, big variance payoff); K=k_large_unit + the unit's bounded MAX_ROUNDS repair rounds above it, or whenever run-level token budget remaining < budget_floor_fraction of the ceiling. Repair rounds count as candidates for the oracle ranking, so rule 4's 'the oracle ranks, not the model' holds by construction at any K. delegate.py run-candidates resolves and ENFORCES this schedule as its default (an explicit --k is an operator override journaled in the verdict pack as a deviation from this decision — never an orchestrator's judgment call); the decision is cited by id, policy:CAND-1, wherever a note used to carry prose.

memory.$comment: Issue #76 — memory is a first-class, policy-resolved budget (MIGRATION_PROMPT.md hard rule 6), not an improvised flag: #73 showed what the one unbounded resource costs — a multi-GB child OOM-killed the session SERVER, not the unit. The ceilings: judge_child_mb bounds each oracle judge/corpus REPL child (untrusted judged code, hence the tighter ceiling); gate_child_mb bounds the toolchain children — the delegate agent, compile gates, wheel build, and the driver's stage workers (repo-trusted, roomier for rustc/LLVM); run_scope_mb is the run-level migration.slice MemoryMax the launch command pins (tools/glv-subagents.md § Memory containment) — it bounds the WHOLE run independently of the session server, it is not a per-child limit; max_corpus_mb is the pre-flight parent-side corpus-retention budget (issue #75). pipeline.py resolve_memory (id MEM-1) emits the decision — decided_by='policy:MEM-1' + policy_version + evidence[] — and delegate.py / oracle.py / pipeline.py enforce it as the DEFAULT of every --mem-limit-mb / --max-corpus-mb flag: an explicit value is an operator override journaled as a deviation from this decision (never an orchestrator's judgment call), 0 disables scoping entirely, and the graceful unscoped fallback when systemd-run is unavailable stays. A cgroup scope breach (child exit 137) is journaled the way token exhaustion is — actor, unit, observed peak, limit — in units[].budget.max_rss_mb + the journal, and resolves as ESC-1 defer (child dies alone -> setup_error -> INCOMPARABLE -> dossier), never a service crash.

rules.title: Stage-0 GO/NO-GO + scope from the recorded projection
rules.decides: approved (go) iff go_no_go.projection.end_to_end_saving_pct >= min_end_to_end_saving_pct AND go_no_go.no_equivalent_deps contains nothing that is still inside the recorded scope (DEP-1 descopes first); else rejected (no-go). Scope = the recorded go_no_go.scope tranche — the minimal set meeting the bar, never 'the repo'.

on_reject.note: NO-GO is a successful terminal state: keep or optimize the Python (ScanCode's original matched its Rust port once given similar effort). Re-enter Stage 0 in a fresh run to grow scope.

rules.title: crate choice from the substitution table
rules.decides: approved with the highest-ranked crate in knowledge/substitutions.json whose 'verified' evidence is 'canonical'/'builtin' or an ISO date within max_verified_age_months of decision time; rejected (module stays Python) when the table has no entry or no candidate carries fresh verification. Never improvises a crate outside the table — that hard rule is unchanged.
rules.evidence_in: python=<module> in the gate evidence[] (or the first word of the gate note)

rules.title: Stage-1 data-structure redesign proposals
rules.decides: approved iff a spike passes the oracle on the golden corpus (spike_verdict=equivalent) AND the matched-corpus benchmark improves by >= min_benchmark_improvement_pct; else rejected — keep the literal shape. The safe default: a proposal without recorded evidence keeps the literal translation; correctness gates apply either way.

rules.title: dependency with no maintained Rust equivalent — descope, don't stop
rules.decides: approved as a descope: the dependency's modules stay Python (dual-build fallback); units inside the module and their transitive dependents are marked fallback_python and dropped from the tranche; the module is removed from go_no_go scope/no_equivalent_deps. Never a substitution, never a halt. 'Never improvise a substitute' remains a hard rule.
rules.evidence_in: module=<python package> in the gate evidence[]

rules.title: escalated units — defer, don't halt
rules.decides: deferred: the unit keeps its Python fallback live, stays 'escalated', and drains into the end-of-run escalation dossier; the backlog continues. Escalation is decoupled from progress — escalation means defer, not halt, and the operator reviews the dossier between runs.

rules.title: mid-run scope changes — conservative reject
rules.decides: rejected: mid-run scope growth is not auto-approved under any level; the request is recorded and surfaced in the run report. The run continues on the already-approved scope; growing scope re-enters Stage 0 in a fresh run (a new projection, not a mid-flight edit).

rules.title: Stage-6 cutover/publish
rules.decides: approved iff shadow_diff_rate <= max_shadow_diff_rate over >= min_shadow_samples AND canary SLOs green for >= min_canary_green_minutes AND rollback actually tested (deploy the old pin, verify, return) — and only at L3 with autonomy.publish_allowed=true. At L2 the gate resolves rejected (publish disabled; the run completes without cutover, dual-build intact). A failed evidence bar at L3 also rejects: no cutover, run continues safely on the fallback.
rules.evidence_in: shadow_diff_rate=<number>, shadow_samples=<int>, canary_green_minutes=<int>, rollback_tested=<true|false> in the gate evidence[]
